newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thailand in power pact with Texaco group.
newsitem.headline: Thailand in power pact with Texaco group.

text.p: State-run Electricity Generating Authority of Thailand (EGAT) said on Friday it has signed an initial power buying agreement with a Texaco-led group under the independent power producer scheme.
The group, known as Tri Energy, is comprised of Texaco, Bangkok-based Banpu Coal Plc and U.S. Black & Veatch, an EGAT official said.
EGAT intends to buy power from the group's 700-megawatt combined-cycle power plant in Ratchaburi, west of Bangkok, for its grid for 20 years, starting May 2000.
The initial agreement will pave the way for Tri Energy to finalise a formal power sale agreement expected to be signed in December, the official said.
The agency plans to buy 4,200 megawatts of power from independent producers by 2002 to meet Thailand's growing demand.
In October, EGAT signed a similar agreement with a consortium comprising Unocal, Westinghouse and Thai Oil.
